headlines.title: Obama says Democrats should have a ‘very clear plan’ on AI policy
headlines.description: Former President Barack Obama urged Democrats to prioritize developing a plan around artificial intelligence, saying that’s what he would be doing if he were running for president in 2028.

headlines.title: Anthropic whistleblower says Congress should let AI companies regulate themselves for now
headlines.description: Former AI researcher Jacob Coxon said any laws Congress passes to regulate the technology need to be able to respond to newly created models quickly.

headlines.title: Florida DMV says it was hacked shortly after major driver’s license breach
headlines.description: Florida’s Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles said Friday that it’s investigating a data breach, making it the second organization that hosts Americans’ driver’s license information to be hacked this month.

headlines.title: North Korea looks abroad for talent in its scheme to infiltrate U.S. companies
headlines.description: North Korea’s surreptitious push to plant employees in U.S. companies has expanded to include remote workers from other countries, such as Iran and Lebanon, according to U.S. government and foreign agencies and several cybersecurity researchers.

headlines.title: Two of the world’s top AI chief executives publicly agree on slowing AI development
headlines.description: The CEOs of two of the world’s leading AI companies are publicly agreeing that the race to build increasingly powerful AI systems needs to be slowed, continuing this week’s cascade of warnings from researchers working on the technology.

headlines.title: Two researchers who left Anthropic and Google warn AI could become ‘uncontrollable’
headlines.description: After Jacob Coxon roiled the AI industry with his viral departure from Anthropic, two more researchers are speaking out about their concerns over AI safety.

headlines.title: Speaker Johnson: ‘I certainly pray’ Trump’s prediction on Iran war ending after midterms is ‘right’
headlines.description: In an interview with Meet the Press, House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) says that the war with Iran is causing higher prices at home and that he hopes and prays that President Trump’s prediction that the fighting would end after the midterm elections is correct.

headlines.title: Pennsylvania woman dies from measles complications, state’s third death this year
headlines.description: The 40-year-old woman died as the U.S. experiences its worst outbreak of the disease in 35 years.

headlines.title: Bessent dared the bond market to ‘bet against’ him. It did — and it appears to be winning.
headlines.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent appears to be losing a tug-of-war with the bond markets he is also trying to influence.

headlines.title: Chinese company releases video of humanoid robot walking off assembly line on its own
headlines.description: Chinese company Xpeng released a video showing its new humanoid robot IRON walking off the assembly line on its own. It’s the latest step in the robot arms race between the U.S. and China that could eventually lead to mass production of the humanoids. NBC News’ Priscilla Thompson reports.

headlines.title: Anthropic Says it Blocked Efforts to Use AI for Biological Weapons
headlines.description: AI company Anthropic says it uncovered multiple attempts by researchers linked to foreign governments to use Claude and other tools for work that could lead to deadly bioweapons. That research was detected and blocked by Anthropic but experts say this kind of example is just the tip of the iceberg. NBC’s Christine Romans reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: More AI researchers warn of AI's threat to humanity
headlines.description: NBC News' Tom Llamas spoke to two more artificial intelligence researchers about the potential threat A.I has to humanity. This comes after AI researcher Jacob Coxon shared a viral tweet saying he believed AI could kill humanity in the next decade. Llamas also spoke to Incoming Professor at UC Berkley Sayash Kapoor who also warns of risk, but says policy proposals and regulations can help prevent further threats.
